reviews.title: Disappointed Viewing
reviews.text:
I’m sure I’d rate this app much higher if I could actually use it to learn. I bought a year subscription w/o knowing that I wouldn’t be able to screen cast it to my TV. It’s way too small on my phone, and still a bit too small to really enjoy and get into from my iPad. 
Please allow my phone to actually play the video while I screen share to HiSense SmartTV 4K from phone; or fix it for iPad. From my iPad to the TV the app and classes play - the downside is that the rewind, play, fast forward icons, and well as time line (the literal line) all stay on the screen while the class is playing. These block me from seeing a lot of the movements and instruction. Or you could allow Google Play Steezy app to be available for my TV. That would be great, I really want to be dancing and learning choreography!!

reviews.title: Free Trial Wasn’t Free
reviews.text:
I signed up for the free 7 day trial and was immediately billed for the entire year. The UX design was confusing and misleading. Upon signing up for the trial, it prompted me to the onboarding questionnaire where I filled out my info and fitness goals, then at the final screen it said I would be billed on 7 days unless canceled. So it was a huge surprise when after I signed up I got a notification from PayPal for a $109 charge that I was not expecting, and that’s not a small transaction.

This is unacceptable because of how misleading the UX was, and that I was not given any notice or warning if my account was not eligible for the trial. Apple has refused to issue a refund and says it’s not eligible, so I want to warn everyone to beware. Don’t sign up if you aren’t sure you want to subscribe.

reviews.title: It would be good if the audio worked
reviews.text: It’s cool but on most of the videos there’s no music audio; you’re redirected to a YouTube video, or in some instances there’s not a YouTube video available to reference, so it kinda defeats the purpose with no sound. Not sure if that’s temporary because I just started using it this week, but unless that were fixed unfortunately it’s really not worth it for me. Other than that, I think it’s a cool idea/app and all of the instructors do a really great job of explaining things, there was only one person’s classes I wasn’t crazy about. Aside from the audio issue, the quality is really good otherwise, so I hope that’s something that’s resolved in the future. But if you don’t mind that or need some concepts explained really well, you’d probably like it. I highly recommend the classes by David Slaney, Kayla Brenda, and Kiira Harper.

reviews.title: Cool
reviews.text: There are thousands of videos with choreography for a variety of different dance styles. You will find slower paced videos that focus more on choreo and others that are much faster and designed to offer an intense workout. I easily keep my heart rate above 140 for the duration of these workouts. It’s more intense than some CrossFit classes I’ve taken, not joking. You could advance your ability to dance quite a bit from inside your own home with a service like this. The price is a tremendous value with that in mind. I just wish they had an API integration for the Apple Watch. There also seems to be some kind of (maybe) integration error that prevents me from signing in on the desktop site with my Apple ID that I used to sign up. So I just airplay my iPhone to my television and that works fine.
